answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a decaying mutual-vouch trellis: every agent may vouch for only a few peers, and each vouch fades unless renewed through real joint work, like a fable where a saffron merchant's word is only as good as the last caravan he actually escorted. A Sybil farm must buy genuine vouches from established agents, and a voucher loses standing if its vouchee misbehaves, so fake identities cost real reputation while honest agents earn vouches free through collaboration.
